title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening notational page (numbered (1)) of a manuscript set of notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex. It reads as follows.

(i) Δ is the category of standard simplices Δ^n = [0,n] ⊂ ℕ with the total order, i.e. the simplex category. Its presheaf category is Δ̂ = Ss = Hom(Δ°, Ens), written Ens_*. 'Ss' is the old Cartan/Kan-era name 'ensembles semi-simpliciaux' for simplicial sets.

(ii) For any category A he sets A_* = Hom(Δ°, A), the simplicial objects, and A^* = Hom(Δ, A), the cosimplicial objects. The page literally writes Ens in the definition of A_*, a slip for A.

(iii) Two duality formulas follow: (A°)^* = (A_*)° and A^* ≃ ((A°)_*)°. Both come from the identity Fun(C,D)° = Fun(C°,D°).

(iv) Two notations for the same category express two viewpoints:
- Ens_* when simplicial sets are seen as 'algebraic structures of a simple type on a set of base objects' (universal algebra);
- Δ̂ or Ss when they are seen as objects or sheaves of a topos.
A vertical marginal footnote justifies the hat notation Δ̂ as a category of presheaves; it is largely illegible.

(v) Programme statement. He proposes to study simplicial sets, as combinatorial equivalents of topological spaces, and their homotopy types through invariants. These invariants are covariant or contravariant functors on Δ̂ = Ens_*. The study is to be systematic, 'in the spirit of universal algebra', covering:
- the structures carried by these invariants;
- operations definable on them that build some complexes from simpler ones.

The following page fixes notation K_* = (K_[n]) and K^* = (K^[n]) and sets up a duality v: A° ≃ B, mainly for A = finitely generated projective left k-modules and B = right ones. It introduces the universal cosimplicial object Δ^*_* (n ↦ Δ^n_*, the Yoneda embedding) and bisimplicial-type objects K^*_* in (A_*)^*.

The purpose is to set up a Dold–Kan / Dold–Puppe style framework of simplicial and cosimplicial k-modules, with duality, in which divided-power (Γ-) functors and the divided-power de Rham complex of a simplicial or cosimplicial object can be constructed functorially.
errors: Definition A_* = Hom(Δ°, Ens) should read Hom(Δ°, A); this is a slip (A^* is likewise written with Ens/'Eh' in the image). It is an author slip, not a mathematical error.
Both duality formulas (A°)^* = (A_*)° and A^* ≃ ((A°)_*)° are correct.

ideas.what: Simplex category Δ and simplicial sets as presheaves Δ̂ = Hom(Δ°,Ens), with a double viewpoint: topos object vs. universal-algebra structure
ideas.modern_name: simplicial sets as presheaf topos / essentially algebraic structures
ideas.where_published: SGA4 (presheaf categories); Pursuing Stacks (Δ̂ notation, test categories)

ideas.what: Simplicial and cosimplicial objects A_*, A^* in a category A, with the opposite-category dualities
Programme: a universal-algebra study of functorial invariants of simplicial sets and of operations on them, producing complexes from simpler ones
ideas.modern_name: functorial/natural operations on simplicial objects; Dold–Puppe non-additive functors; cohomology operations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold–Puppe (1961), Eilenberg–MacLane; later Illusie (Complexe cotangent), Quillen

missed.claim: Grothendieck announces a systematic 'universal algebra' study of invariants of simplicial sets (functors on Δ̂) and of the operations between them. This page only states the programme; no content is given. In the context of the 1976 divided-power de Rham lecture, it is an announced framework rather than a result.
missed.quote: Nous avons ici en vue une étude systématique, dans l'esprit de l'algèbre universelle, de ces invariants, (qui sont donc des foncteurs sur Δ̂=Ens_*) de leurs structures et des opérations qui peuvent être définies sur elles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only marginally relevant. It foreshadows the functorial/derived approach to divided-power de Rham cohomology (Illusie, Bhatt's derived de Rham, animated rings), but the page itself contains no specific construction.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely notational and programmatic opening page with standard definitions. The only mildly interesting feature is that it documents Grothendieck using the Δ̂ / Ens_* double viewpoint and a 'universal algebra' programme in 1975–76, before Pursuing Stacks.
transcription_corrections: Line 'A_* = Hom(Δ°, Ens)': the image indeed shows Ens (and 'Eh(s)' for A^*), but the intended meaning is A; this should be flagged.

The quoted terms are 'objets ½ simpliciaux' resp. '½ cosimpliciaux'. The '½' is Grothendieck's abbreviation for 'semi-' (cf. the previous page, 'Notations ½ simpliciales'), and the transcription omits it.
The insertion above 'cat. opposée' (rendered {+[?]+}) is illegible; it may be a word such as 'variance' or 'usuelle'.
'via des invariants qui, par leur nature, qui en dépendent' probably reads 'invariants pris par leur nature, qui en dépendent de façon covariante ou contravariante'.
Marginal date '1975 ou 1976' at the top left is correctly read.
